items.title: Edwin "Squirrel" Ashcraft Interview, 1961-08-16
items.q: They played many things like, well, even Napoleon and Miff were talking about it

ctx.x: Would you call the loudness a feature of dynamics, or just they played loud all the time?

Fortunately, they used dynamics. They played in contrast. They played many things like, well, even Napoleon and Miff were talking about it, although they weren't doing much about it before. They called it underwater. They'd go down to the punny trombone underwater, was their phrase. And they would get way down.

And frequently it would lead to a breathing kind of effect, where the soft playing would be an intake of breath, and then a little later on you'd let it all out. Yeah. Although the phrase might be pretty long, that is, dynamics might extend 16 bars, you thought of it sometimes as a breathing effect as well as underwater and out.
